headline: Manitoba Provincial Park Vehicle Permits
reservation: A valid Manitoba Provincial Park vehicle permit is required for entry and must be purchased online or at authorized retailers before arrival. While the park is open for day use, campsites and the resort within the Hecla historic village often sell out during the summer months and require early booking through the Parks Reservation Service.

days.title: Icelandic Heritage and Village Life

stops.name: Hecla Historic Village
stops.detail: Explore the restored 19th-century buildings, including the schoolhouse and church, established by Icelandic settlers.

stops.name: Gull Harbour Marina
stops.detail: Walk the docks of this sheltered harbor, which serves as the primary hub for boating on Lake Winnipeg's northern basin.

days.driving: Allow 30–45 minutes for local park roads; speeds are reduced for wildlife safety.
days.note: The village is a living community; please respect private property while viewing historical sites.

days.title: Marshlands and Avian Observation

stops.name: Grassy Narrows Marsh
stops.detail: Traverse the boardwalks and viewing towers to spot pelicans, terns, and occasionally moose in the wetlands.

stops.name: Hecla Island Causeway
stops.detail: Stop at the pull-outs along the causeway for a panoramic view of the marsh and Lake Winnipeg.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for exploring the marsh access roads; gravel surfaces may be uneven.
days.note: Early morning offers the best chance for wildlife sightings before temperatures rise.

days.title: North Point Cliffs and Lighthouses
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the North Point Trailhead

stops.name: North Point Lighthouse
stops.detail: Hike the forested trail to the historic lighthouse overlooking the limestone cliffs and the vast lake.

stops.name: Sunset Beach
stops.detail: Enjoy the limestone cobble shores and clear water on the quieter western side of the island.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; the road to North Point is well-maintained but ends in a trailhead parking lot.
days.note: The cliffs are fragile; stay on marked paths to prevent erosion and for personal safety.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: Primary parking is found at Hecla Village, Gull Harbour, and the North Point trailhead. On weekends, the Gull Harbour area can become busy with boat trailers, so consider early arrival.

intel.title: Island Coverage
intel.text: Cellular reception is generally stable near Hecla Village and the resort area. However, signal strength can be intermittent on the North Point trails and in the Grassy Narrows marshland.

intel.title: Last Stops
intel.text: Fuel is available in Riverton before crossing the causeway. There are no traditional gas stations on the island itself, though limited marine fuel may be found at the marina.

intel.title: Seasonal Shifts
intel.text: The park remains open in winter for cross-country skiing, but many heritage buildings and the marina operate only from late May through September.

intel.title: Causeway Transit
intel.text: Hecla Island is connected to the mainland by a paved causeway on Highway 8. High winds on Lake Winnipeg can occasionally cause spray or debris on the road; drive with caution.

plan.arrival: Pick up a rental at Winnipeg (YWG) and drive north through Gimli; buy groceries in Gimli or Riverton as the island has limited convenience options.
plan.vehicle: A standard passenger car is perfectly suitable for the paved roads of Hecla, though an SUV provides a smoother ride on the Grindstone gravel side-trips.
plan.goldenHour: The North Point limestone cliffs offer a striking white backdrop for the orange hues of a Lake Winnipeg sunset.
